patch:
diff --git a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
index 1267cc2..8d38606 100644
--- a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
+++ b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
@@ -57,6 +57,21 @@ Rules:
 - true, echo, printf, pwd, directory listings, and display-only reads are not completion checks.
 - Use replan when the current approach is wrong. Use stop only when blocked, unsafe, or impossible.
 - Keep rationale short. State the current fact and why the selected action changes or proves it.
+- Budget turns deliberately. Use the first turns to read the task's exact requirements (paths, file
+  names, formats, CLI/API names, thresholds) and the relevant inputs, then implement. Pack up to
+  four related commands into each execute batch instead of spending a turn per command. Do not
+  stop after a stop-worthy first failure: diagnose the error output and try a different approach.
+- Hidden acceptance tests will check the final state of the sandbox against the ORIGINAL TASK
+  literally. Before finish, re-read the task and list every concrete deliverable: exact output
+  path, exact filename, format, schema, and value range. Make sure each exists exactly as
+  specified, that services are left running if the task needs them, and that nothing required
+  was left in a temporary or intermediate location.
+- Do not rely on one happy-path run. Completion checks should exercise the deliverable the way an
+  independent test would: run it on the real inputs, compare against an independent reference or
+  known expected values, assert exact formats and counts, and probe at least one edge case.
+  A check that only reruns the code you wrote against your own assumptions is weak evidence.
+- If a time-consuming job is needed (build, training, large conversion), start it early, run
+  it with a timeout inside the command limit or in the background with logs, and poll it.
 """.strip()
 
 _REVIEW_RULES = """
